# Technical Guide to Watermark Removal in Image Editing

## Basic Clone Stamp Method
1. Open your image in an editing program with clone stamp functionality
2. Zoom in to the watermarked area for precision
3. Select the clone stamp tool
4. Choose an appropriate brush size slightly larger than parts of the watermark
5. Hold Alt/Option and click on a clean area near the watermark to sample it
6. Carefully paint over the watermark, resampling clean areas as needed
7. Adjust opacity and flow settings for more natural blending
8. Work in small sections, frequently resampling from different areas

## Content-Aware Fill Approach
1. Select the watermarked area using a selection tool
2. Expand the selection by 2-3 pixels to ensure complete coverage
3. Use the content-aware fill function (or equivalent)
4. Adjust the sampling parameters if available
5. Apply and assess the result
6. For imperfect results, try multiple smaller selections instead of one large one

## Healing Brush Technique
1. Select the healing brush tool
2. Choose a brush size appropriate for the watermark elements
3. Sample from unmarked areas with similar texture and color
4. Paint over the watermark in short strokes
5. Allow the algorithm to blend each stroke before continuing

## Advanced Frequency Separation
1. Duplicate your image into multiple layers
2. Apply Gaussian blur to one layer (5-10px depending on image size)
3. Use "Apply Image" with "Subtract" mode on another layer
4. Add a gray fill layer with "Linear Light" blending
5. Edit the texture layer to remove high-frequency watermark elements
6. Edit the color layer to address any remaining color inconsistencies

These techniques work best on simple watermarks and may require combining multiple approaches for optimal results.
